description: One of the two great empires flanking Marrenhold. The beastkin are anthropomorphic hybrids of many animals -- countless beast-tribes, the hyenadin among them -- welded into a single empire by conquest. (They are distinct from the dragonkin, who are dragon-blooded, cursed, and unaffiliated with any empire.) Beastkin culture is martial and hierarchical to its core: tribes and individuals establish rank through ritual martial duels, and the empire has grown by absorbing beaten tribes into its pecking-order. Strength, proven in the duel, is the measure of worth.
rules: The empire expands by conquest and absorption; internal order is kept by dueling hierarchy. As it mobilizes toward war with the Geistkin Empire, its beast-tribes range wider and hungrier -- and the hyenadin, a scavenger-tribe within it, fall on the dragonkin at the mesa. A defense-bound people cannot repel them (fighting back in earnest deepens the curse); Kaelen's fire kills many attackers but is not enough, and it kills him. Tomas, having left, returns too late to discover the aftermath, not to fight the battle. The war-summons that draws Tomas away and the hyenadin raid that destroys the fold share a single root: Beastkin aggression.

details.The hyenadin: Hyena-beastkin, a scavenger-tribe of the Beastkin Empire. Rival and hostile to the dragonkin; the aggressors who slaughter the fold at the mesa. Scavenger-predators who prey on the weak, drawn to a cursed, defense-bound people who cannot strike back without damning themselves -- the curse's defense-only law turned into a hunting weakness. Seeded circling the mesa during the stay; they strike once Tomas (a fighter who could strike without curse-cost) has gone.
details.Duels and pecking-order: Rank and worth are decided by ritual martial combat; conquest is how the empire grows and how beaten tribes are folded into the hierarchy. A whole civilization organized around the duel.
details.Relation to the war: Their martial expansion is one half of the Geistkin-Beastkin conflict whose brink drives the war-summons. The empire's mobilization is what pushes the hyenadin outward against the dragonkin -- so the massacre and the war are the same aggression, at two scales.
details.Open / to build later: The Beastkin emperor and leadership; which other beast-tribes matter; how organized the hyenadin raid is (a war-band, an opportunistic pack); the empire's deeper culture and its casus belli with the Geistkin.
